title: macOS BlueParrott button via CoreBluetooth
description:
## Design Document
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md

## Overview
Detect BlueParrott multifunction-button events on macOS by reimplementing the
iOS BPHeadset SDK's BLE GATT integration directly on CoreBluetooth, since the
SDK xcframework ships iOS-only slices. Replaces the current (broken) CoreAudio
mute-proxy trigger that never sees the button.

- Phase A: a DEBUG-only collector that captures the proprietary GATT protocol
  (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, button-event byte format) by
  instrumenting the working iOS SDK, plus an App-Mode persistence experiment
  that decides Phase B's scope.
- Phase B: a macOS CoreBluetooth client + pure byte parser feeding the existing
  BlueParrottButtonDelegate / HeadsetRemoteCommandManager state machine unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. macOS button down starts recording and up stops+sends, matching iOS PTT behavior.
2. macOS tap / double-tap / long-press map to the same actions as iOS
   (HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift:626-665).
3. BlueParrottEventParser unit tests pass against the captured real-device byte
   sequences for all five gestures, and return nil for empty/unknown payloads.
4. Connect/retry/re-arm unit tests pass with a faked BLECentral (no hardware).
5. Out-of-range disconnect returns the state machine to ready and reconnects
   automatically when the headset returns.
6. make build-mac (scheme VoiceCodeMac) succeeds with
   com.apple.security.device.bluetooth added; make build (iOS) is unchanged.
7. The Phase A collector (BPSniffer) is absent from release builds
   (#if DEBUG verified by a release-config build).
8. make test-mac passes (runs the new macOS VoiceCodeMacTests) and make test
   still passes (iOS suite, no regression).

title: Build Phase A1 DEBUG GATT collector (BPSniffer) to capture the BlueParrott protocol
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase A1 — passive observer)

## Context
Unblocking step. The proprietary GATT protocol (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, per-gesture byte format) is not in the public SDK header — capture it by instrumenting the working iOS BPHeadset SDK.

## Requirements
- [ ] New `BPSniffer.swift`, gated `#if DEBUG && os(iOS)`
- [ ] Swizzle `CBPeripheral.writeValue(_:for:type:)` → log characteristic UUID + payload hex
- [ ] Discover the SDK's peripheral delegate at runtime and swizzle `peripheral:didUpdateValueForCharacteristic:` → log UUID + value hex
- [ ] Route all output through `LogManager.shared.log(category: "BPSniff")`
- [ ] Install the hook from a DEBUG entry point when BlueParrott is enabled
- [ ] On hardware: capture the App-Mode enable write (char + bytes) and each gesture's notification (char + bytes) for down/up/tap/double-tap/long-press

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's Code Examples (BPSniffer). Objective-C runtime method swizzling.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BPSniffer.swift`
- Dependencies: none (iOS already has the BLE entitlement and links the working SDK)

## Verification
- [ ] Manual (hardware): iOS DEBUG build, enable BlueParrott, press all 5 gestures → "BPSniff" logs show the enable-write and per-gesture bytes
- [ ] Release-config build confirms `BPSniffer` is compiled out

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #7 (collector absent from release builds); produces the captured bytes that epic #3 depends on.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: "Add macOS Bluetooth entitlement and usage description".

title: Wire BlueParrott button events: subscribe, parse, dispatch, conditional App-Mode enable
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B happy path + byte parser)

## Context
Completes the macOS client on top of the core/lifecycle task: subscribe to the button-event characteristic, parse via `BlueParrottEventParser`, dispatch to the delegate, and enable App Mode only when the headset doesn't persist it. (Split from the original combined client task.)

## Requirements
- [ ] On connect: subscribe to the button-event characteristic (UUID from the A1 capture)
- [ ] Write `appModeEnablePayload` only if App Mode is not persistent (per the persistence experiment)
- [ ] In `bleDidUpdateButtonValue`: parse via `BlueParrottEventParser`, dispatch to `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` on the main queue; log unknown payloads (never misclassify)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's happy-path example.
- Files to modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (event extension)
- Dependencies: BLE core/lifecycle task, A1 capture (characteristic UUID + enable payload), persistence experiment, BlueParrottEventParser

## Verification
- [ ] Unit test with `FakeBLECentral` + `DelegateSpy`: a button-down notification → delegate call; unknown payload → no dispatch
- [ ] Runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Contributes to epic #1, #2, #5.

title: Add macOS Bluetooth entitlement and usage description
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Entitlements & Info.plist)

## Context
The macOS sandbox blocks CoreBluetooth without the Bluetooth device entitlement. Required before any macOS BLE work (the persistence experiment and the Phase B client).

## Requirements
- [ ] Add `com.apple.security.device.bluetooth` to `VoiceCodeMac.entitlements`
- [ ] Ensure `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` applies to the macOS target

## Technical Approach
- Files to modify: `ios/VoiceCodeMac/VoiceCodeMac.entitlements`, `ios/project.yml`
- Dependencies: none

## Verification
- [ ] `make build-mac` (scheme VoiceCodeMac) succeeds with the entitlement present
- [ ] `make build` (iOS) is unchanged

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #6.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: "Build Phase A1 DEBUG GATT collector (BPSniffer)".

title: Build A2 GATT explorer and run the App-Mode persistence experiment
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase A2 + Key experiment)

## Context
Determine whether App/SDK mode is persisted on the headset hardware. The result decides whether the Phase B client must replay the App-Mode enable handshake or can simply connect + subscribe.

## Requirements
- [ ] DEBUG `CBCentralManager` explorer: scan service 95665a00-…, enumerate services/characteristics + properties, subscribe to all notifiers, log notification hex
- [ ] Make the explorer runnable on macOS (requires the Bluetooth entitlement)
- [ ] Enable App Mode once via the iOS SDK, power-cycle/reconnect, then observe from macOS whether button notifications still flow with no re-handshake
- [ ] Record the decision (persistent / not persistent) on this issue and in the design doc

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's Phase A2 description. Note the explorer must be cross-platform (the doc's Files table places A2 in the iOS-only BPSniffer; it must also run on macOS for this experiment).
- Dependencies: macOS Bluetooth entitlement task

## Verification
- [ ] Manual (hardware): documented observation of persistent vs not persistent

## Acceptance Criteria
Informs the #1/#2 implementation path; gates the Phase B client (whether `writeAppModeEnable` is needed).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: the A1 collector and the parser (after the entitlement lands).

title: Implement BlueParrottEventParser (pure byte→event) with unit tests
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (byte parser) + #4-verification-strategy

## Context
Pure decode of a notification payload to a logical gesture — the unit-testable core of the macOS client. Opcode constants come from the A1 capture.

## Requirements
- [ ] `BlueParrottButtonEvent` enum (down/up/tap/doubleTap/longPress)
- [ ] `BlueParrottEventParser.parse(Data) -> BlueParrottButtonEvent?`, returning nil for empty/unknown payloads
- [ ] Populate the opcode table from the captured bytes (A1)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's parser example.
- New files: parser in `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (or a small dedicated file)
- Dependencies: A1 collector (captured byte format)

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests: each gesture decodes to the right event; empty payload → nil; unknown opcode → nil — using the captured real-device byte sequences

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #3.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: the A2 / persistence experiment (after the A1 capture).

title: Implement BlueParrottBLEManager macOS CoreBluetooth client with tests
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B + API Design) + #4-verification-strategy

## Context
The macOS CoreBluetooth client that connects, optionally enables App Mode, subscribes to button events, parses them, and emits `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` — the replacement event source for the mute proxy.

## Requirements
- [ ] `BLECentral` / `BLECentralEvents` test seam + a real `CBCentralManager`-backed adapter that delivers callbacks on the main queue
- [ ] Connect/retry/re-arm state machine mirroring the iOS manager (fast retries → infinite 30s slow retry; `maxRetries = 5`; DEBUG `testInSlowRetry` hook)
- [ ] On connect: subscribe to the button-event characteristic; write `appModeEnablePayload` only if App Mode is not persistent (per the experiment)
- [ ] Parse notifications via `BlueParrottEventParser`; dispatch to `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` on the main queue
- [ ] Handle `CBManagerState` (poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's API Design + happy/error-path examples; use the characteristic UUIDs and handshake payload from A1.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift`
- Dependencies: A1 collector, macOS entitlement, persistence experiment, BlueParrottEventParser

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests with `FakeBLECentral` + `DelegateSpy`: transient failure → slow-retry fallback; button-down → delegate call
- [ ] Test file is `#if os(macOS)` and added to the iOS `VoiceCodeTests` `excludes`; runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #4 (retry/state-machine tests); contributes to #1/#2/#5.
delete_reason: Split into voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.9 (core/lifecycle) and voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.10 (subscribe/parse/dispatch) — original task too large for one session

title: Rewire macOS HeadsetRemoteCommandManager to drive BlueParrottBLEManager
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Component Interactions) + Implementation Notes

## Context
Swap the macOS button source from `BluetoothAudioMonitor` to `BlueParrottBLEManager`, keeping the existing state mapping untouched so iOS and macOS converge on one downstream path.

## Requirements
- [ ] macOS: instantiate and drive `BlueParrottBLEManager` from `HeadsetRemoteCommandManager`, gated by `settings.blueParrottEnabled`, set as its delegate
- [ ] State mapping (HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift:626-665) unchanged

## Technical Approach
- Files to modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift`
- Dependencies: BlueParrottBLEManager

## Verification
- [ ] Integration test (macOS): a BLEManager-sourced down/up produces record → stop+send
- [ ] Existing `HeadsetRemoteCommandManagerTests` still pass

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #1, #2, #5.

title: Retire BluetoothAudioMonitor as the macOS button trigger
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#implementation-notes + #rollback-strategy

## Context
Once the CoreBluetooth path reaches parity, remove the unreliable CoreAudio mute proxy as the button trigger.

## Requirements
- [ ] Remove the `BluetoothAudioMonitor` button-trigger wiring from `HeadsetRemoteCommandManager` (macOS)
- [ ] Decide whether to keep `BluetoothAudioMonitor` for a separate mic-mute feature or remove it entirely
- [ ] Update or retire `BluetoothAudioMonitorTests` accordingly

## Technical Approach
- Files to modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift`, `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BluetoothAudioMonitor.swift` (+ tests)
- Dependencies: HeadsetRemoteCommandManager rewire (parity confirmed)

## Verification
- [ ] `make test-mac` and `make test` pass
- [ ] Manual: the button still works via the BLE path after removal

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #8 (no regressions); satisfies goal "retire BluetoothAudioMonitor as the macOS button trigger".

title: Manual hardware validation of the full macOS hands-free loop
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#4-verification-strategy (manual checklist + acceptance criteria)

## Context
End-to-end confirmation on real hardware that the macOS button drives the full hands-free loop.

## Requirements
- [ ] PTT loop: button down → record, up → send, hear TTS response
- [ ] tap / double-tap / long-press match the iOS mappings
- [ ] Out-of-range disconnect → state returns to ready; auto-reconnect when back in range

## Technical Approach
Hardware test against the doc's manual checklist. Record the validated firmware version.
- Dependencies: HeadsetRemoteCommandManager rewire

## Verification
- [ ] All manual checklist items pass on the target firmware

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #1, #2, #5.

title: Implement BlueParrottBLEManager core: CoreBluetooth seam, adapter, connect/retry state machine
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase B + API Design)

## Context
The macOS client's foundation — the CoreBluetooth abstraction plus the connect/retry/re-arm lifecycle — split from event handling so it is a single focused unit. Mirrors the iOS manager's structure. (Split from the original combined client task.)

## Requirements
- [ ] `BlueParrottBLEManager` (macOS) skeleton: `@Published` connection state, `BlueParrottButtonDelegate` hookup point
- [ ] `BLECentral` / `BLECentralEvents` test seam + a real `CBCentralManager`-backed adapter that delivers callbacks on the main queue and wires `centralDelegate = self`
- [ ] Scan for service 95665a00-…, connect, discover services
- [ ] Connect/retry/re-arm state machine mirroring iOS (fast retries → infinite 30s slow retry; `maxRetries = 5`; DEBUG `testInSlowRetry` hook)
- [ ] Handle `CBManagerState` (poweredOff/resetting/unauthorized/unsupported)

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's API Design + error-path example. The service UUID is known from the header; characteristic-level subscribe/parse is the sibling task.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift` (skeleton + lifecycle)
- Dependencies: macOS Bluetooth entitlement

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests with `FakeBLECentral`: transient connect failure → slow-retry fallback; `CBManagerState` handling
- [ ] Test file is `#if os(macOS)` and added to the iOS `VoiceCodeTests` `excludes`; runs under `make test-mac`

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #4 (connect/retry/re-arm tests with a faked BLECentral).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: A1 collector, A2/persistence experiment, and the parser (after the entitlement lands).
